Students work closely with an industry sponsor, under the mentorship of a faculty advisor to execute the research proposal that was developed in CMGT 8700 . The students' pre-approved proposal outlines the project scope, goals, methods, and deliverables that forms the basis for this course. This course is intended to assess the students' ability to integrate the skills and knowledge gained from the Program with their individual work experience and apply these in a real-world context. In conjunction with an industry sponsor, the student solves a technical problem relating to construction. definitions.E4:
Understood. You’re in the **Construction Management Bachelor of Technology**, a degree-completion program offered full- or part-time, in person at the Burnaby campus. Its curriculum includes courses such as **CMGT 7190 — Construction Planning and Controls** and **CMGT 7330 — Finance for Construction Managers**, alongside management electives, Liberal Studies, and a final industry project.

Program details: https://www.bcit.ca/programs/construction-management-bachelor-of-technology-full-time-part-time-8800btech/
definitions.E1:
No. For graduation, you must complete:

- **CMGT 8700 — Industry Based Project Proposal**
- Then choose **one** final project: **CMGT 8800 — Industry Based Project** or **CMGT 8810 — Industry Based Project**

Both final-project options require department approval. You do not need to complete both.

[Construction Management program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/construction-management-bachelor-of-technology-full-time-part-time-8800btech/)
definitions.E2:
No. You cannot skip both. For graduation, you must complete **CMGT 8700 — Industry Based Project Proposal**, followed by **one** of these final projects:

- **CMGT 8800 — Industry Based Project**
- **CMGT 8810 — Industry Based Project**

The chosen final project requires department approval.

[View program details](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/construction-management-bachelor-of-technology-full-time-part-time-8800btech/)
